The Insurance Company has preferred this appeal against the Judgment and Award dated 25th July, 2019 passed in MVC No.349 of 2013 by the Principal Senior Civil Judge and Additional MACT, Hubballi (for brevity hereinafter referred to as 'the  3 Tribunal') questioning the liability of Insurance Company and also quantum of compensation.
2. For the sake of convenience, parties in this appeal are referred to as per their rank and status before the Tribunal.

sentences.text:
Brief facts of the petition filed by the petitioners before the Tribunal, are:
 On 9th April, 2013, Sunil, the son of Aravind Apte, was a passenger on the motorcycle with Registration No. KA-25/Y- 0784, being driven by the respondent No.1-Karibasaveshwar Jadekar.

While en-route Dharwad to Hubballi via by-pass road,
specifically near Micro Finish Factory, Itigatti, around 2:15 am,
the motorcyclist, in a reckless and negligent manner,
jeopardized human safety and lost control of the vehicle.

Consequently, both individuals were thrown off the motorcycle,
sustaining injuries.
They were promptly transported to Lifeline 24/7 and ICU Hospital in Hubballi.
Here, Sunil received inpatient care from the 9th to 14th April, 2013.
Tragically, due to a severe head injury accompanied by brainstem dysfunction, he  4 succumbed to injuries on 14th April, 2013, while still under hospital care.
4.1 The petitioners assert that they spared no effort in their attempt to secure proper treatment for their beloved son- Sunil, incurring medical expenses amounting to Rs.1,00,000/-.
Regrettably, despite their earnest endeavour, these attempts proved futile.
Prior to this devastating accident, the deceased enjoyed robust health.

He held the position of a Development Officer at ING Life Insurance Company, earning a monthly salary The Divisional Manager vs Sri. Aravind Gajanan Apte on 15 September, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/29919585/
3 of Rs.23,000/-.

entities.text: Divisional Manager vs Sri. Aravind Gajanan Apte
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Notably, he was the sole breadwinner for the petitioners' family.
In this capacity, he was responsible for providing financial support to his elderly parents.
The petitioner's elder brother, residing separately with his own family and children, did not share this burden.
4.2 The sudden loss of the family's primary source of income has subjected the petitioners to considerable mental anguish and distress.
Their grief is further compounded by the absence of their cherished son's love and care.
Importantly, at the time of the accident, the deceased was 27 years old, known  5 for his brilliance, diligence, and exemplary qualities.
Additionally, he was on the cusp of marriage, which adds to the tragedy of his untimely passing.
4.3 Based on these compelling circumstances, the petitioners seek rightful compensation.
Their claim rests on the premise that the negligent and reckless conduct of the rider of motorcycle-Karibasaveshwar Jadekar, directly contributed to the demise of Sunil.
The compensation sought encompasses medical expenses, loss of Sunil's income, and the profound emotional distress endured by the petitioners due to the sudden loss of their son.

5. On service of Notice, respondents 1 to 3 appeared through their counsel and respondents 2 and 3 have filed The Divisional Manager vs Sri. Aravind Gajanan Apte on 15 September, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/29919585/
4 objections to the main petition.

sentences.text: 6. Respondent No.2 has acknowledged both the accident in question and the unfortunate demise of Sunil.

In the statement of objections provided by respondent No.2, it is conveyed that he is the rightful owner of the motorcycle with Registration No.
KA-25/Y-0784.
This motorcycle was insured with respondent  6 No.3-Insurance Company at the time of the accident.

Respondent No.2 further submits that if the Court arrives at the determination that he is indeed liable to provide compensation,
he suggests that the responsibility for compensation be transferred to respondent No.3-Insurance Company.

Moreover,
respondent No.2 has refuted the assertions presented in the claim petition.

He regards these statements as being baseless,
lacking merit, and intended solely to cause annoyance or trouble.
The respondent No.2 denied the averments made in the claim petition as false, frivolous and vexatious and on these grounds, has requested dismissal of the petition.

7. The core of the statement of objections provided by Respondent No.3-Insurance Company centers around the contention that the purported accident did not result from any negligence on the part of the motorcycle's rider.

According to Respondent No.3-Insurance Company, the petitioners have intentionally omitted crucial and pertinent facts while presenting The Divisional Manager vs Sri. Aravind Gajanan Apte on 15 September, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/29919585/
5 their case to the Court.

entities.text: Divisional Manager vs Sri. Aravind Gajanan Apte
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: This, it is claimed, is an effort to unjustly profit by involving Respondent No.1, who is the insurer  7 of the vehicle owned by Respondent No.2.
The petitioners are alleged to have failed in supplying substantial and essential details that would corroborate their claim against Respondent No.3.
In fact, false accusations have been made against Respondent No.3 as well.
7.1. Respondent No.3-Insurance Company asserts that the motorcycle's rider did not possess a valid and effective driving license at the relevant time.
It is further put forward that Respondent No.2, the owner of the motorcycle, knowingly and deliberately handed over the vehicle's possession to the rider.
As a result, it is contended that, Respondent No.2 breached the policy's terms and conditions and violated its stipulations.
7.2. Respondent No.2 is also accused of not promptly notifying the insurer about the accident, nor did they provide any information concerning the incident within the prescribed timeframe.

In an effort to clarify the actual matter of contention between the involved parties, Respondent No.2 was requested to produce vehicular documents, including the Registration  8 Certificate, and other pertinent records.

Hence, the respondent The Divisional Manager vs Sri. Aravind Gajanan Apte on 15 September, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/29919585/
6 No.3-Insurance Company, has denied all the averments made in the claim petition as false and sought for dismissal of petition.

8. Based on the above pleadings, the Tribunal has framed the following issues:
 "(1) Whether the petitioners prove that deceased by  name Sunil S/o Aravind Apte was died in a road  traffic accident on 09.04.2013 at 8.50 pm on Hubli  Dharwad By-pass near Micro Finish Factory near  Itigatti, due to rash and negligent riding of the  motorcycle No.KA/-25-Y-0784 by its rider?
(2) Whether the petitioner is entitled for the  compensation?
If so what amount, from whom?
And  what interest?

(3) What order or Award?"
 9.
In order to substantiate their case, petitioner No.1 got himself examined as PW1 and got marked twelve documents as Exhibits P1 to P12.

Respondent No.3-Insurance Company got examined the Senior Manager of Kotak Mahindra Insurance,
Hubballi as RW1; Assistant Administrative Officer of respondent No.3-Insurance Company as RW2; Sri Ramanagouda A Hatti,
 9 Deputy Superintendent of Police, Rural Dharwad, as RW3; Dr.
Yallappa B. Dambal as RW4; and Mahammad Basha, Engineer,
Toll Plaza, Bankapur, as RW5 and got marked ten documents as per Exhibits R1 to R10.

10 . Upon hearing arguments on both sides, the Tribunal has given its finding as under:

7  Issue No.1: In the affirmative.
 Issue No.2: Partly in the affirmative.

11. In view of the above finding, Tribunal allowed the claim petition in part and awarded compensation of Rs.20,16,705/- with interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of petition till its realisation.
12. Being aggrieved by the judgment and award passed by the Tribunal, the Insurance Company has preferred this appeal.

13. Learned counsel representing the appellant Insurance Company has presented his arguments, contending that the  10 judgment and award passed by the Tribunal are in direct contradiction to both law and the material presented in the case record.
It is the counsel's assertion that the accident was caused by the negligent operation of the motorcycle by the deceased-Sunil Aravind Apte.
However, in an effort to wrongly implicate the appellant-Insurance Company, Karibasaveshwar S/o Mohan Jadekar has been falsely identified as the motorcycle's rider.

The counsel posits that the Tribunal's judgment and award are the result of fraudulent actions and misrepresentations orchestrated by petitioners in collusion with respondents 1 and 2, the Investigating Officer of the crime, and The Divisional Manager vs Sri. Aravind Gajanan Apte on 15 September, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/29919585/
8 the authorities at Lifeline Hospital, Hubballi.
 13.1.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Furthermore, the counsel argues that there exists a delay of one day in filing the complaint.
The accident occurred on 09th April, 2013, at 8:50 pm, yet the complaint was lodged on 10th April, 2013, at 8:05 pm.

The complaint, submitted by an individual named Vinayak Desai, alleges that while he was driving a car with registration No. KA-22/N-7112 from Narendra Toll Gate towards Hubballi on Hubballi-Dharwad By-pass Road, a  11 motorcycle overtaken by its rider caused the accident near Micro Finish Factory.

Complainant states that he transported both the rider and the pillion rider of the motorcycle to Lifeline Hospital,
Hubballi, and returned home.
The next day, he found them still receiving treatment as indoor patients, prompting his belated complaint.

However, evidence presented before the Tribunal has established that respondent No.1-Karibasaveshwar Jadekar,
was not admitted to Lifeline Hospital as an inpatient.
Despite this crucial aspect being proven, the Tribunal disregarded this evidence and ruled that the deceased was a pillion rider, and the motorcycle was operated by respondent No.1-Jadekar.
This oversight, according to the counsel, has led to a miscarriage of justice.
The counsel contends that the Tribunal failed to adequately assess the evidence on record in alignment with legal principles and factual accuracy.

sentences.text: The counsel has reiterated the claims stated in the memorandum of appeal and calls for the dismissal of the claim petition.

14. Per contra, learned counsel appearing for the respondent-claimants submitted that the Tribunal has appreciated the evidence on record in accordance with law and facts and there are no grounds to interfere with the impugned judgment and award passed by the Tribunal and accordingly,
sought for dismissal of this appeal.

15. Having heard the arguments advanced by both sides and on perusal of records, the following points would arise for our consideration:
 1.

Whether the appellant-Insurance Company has  made out a ground to interfere with the  impugned judgment and award as to the finding  given by the Tribunal regarding the rash and  negligent act on the part of the offending  motorcycle No.KA-25/Y-0784 by its rider?
 2. What Order or Award?

Our finding to the above points are as under:

17 . We have carefully examined the material placed before this Court.

On the basis of the complaint filed by one Vinayak Bheemrao Desai, Dharwad Rural Police have registered Crime No.0090 of 2013 against the rider of motorcycle bearing No.KA-25/Y-0784 for commission of offence under Sections 337,
279, 338 of Indian Penal Code and submitted First Information Report to the Court.

Thereafter, police have rushed to the spot,
conducted spot panchanama in the presence of panchas and prepared rough sketch on the spot.

The vehicle in question involved in the accident was examined by the Motor Vehicle Inspector; Investigation Officer has recorded the statement of witnesses; obtained post-mortem report and on thorough investigation, Investigating Officer has submitted the charge- sheet against the rider of the motorcycle bearing registration No.KA-25/Y-0784 for commission of offence punishable under Sections 279, 337, 304A of Indian Penal Code read with Section  14 134 and 187 of the Motor Vehicles Act.
Apart from this documentary evidence, petitioners also adduced oral evidence of PW1-Aravind Apte.
During the course of cross-examination of PW1, the respondents have not questioned as to the charge sheet submitted against the rider of the offending vehicle.

RW1-Anand Mahadevappa Sajjan, Senior Manager,
Kotak Mahindra Insurance Company, Hubballi has stated in his evidence that the material submitted to this Court has been meticulously examined.
Based on the complaint lodged by Vinayak Bheemrao Desai, Dharwad Rural Police initiated Criminal Case No.0090 of 2013 against the motorcyclist with Licence Plate No.KA-25/Y-0784.
This action was taken for alleged violations under Sections 337, 279, and 338 of the Indian Penal Code.
Subsequently, a First Information Report was submitted to the Court.
19 . Following this, the police, by arriving at the scene and conducting a spot inspection in the presence of witnesses (panchas), prepared a rough sketch.
The vehicle involved in the accident underwent examination by a Motor Vehicle Inspector.

15 The Investigation Officer also obtained witness statements, post- mortem reports, and engaged in thorough investigation, the Investigation Officer proceeded to file a charge sheet against the motorcyclist operating the vehicle with License Plate No.KA- 25/Y-0784.

The charges included offences punishable under Sections 279, 337, and 304A of the Indian Penal Code, in conjunction with Sections 134 and 187 of the Motor Vehicles Act.
 20.
In addition to this documentary evidence, the petitioners presented oral evidence through PW1-Aravind Apte.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Remarkably, during the cross-examination of PW1, the respondents did not contest or inquire about the charge sheet that had been filed against the motorcyclist responsible for the incident as the deceased-Sunil Apte was working along with him in ING Vysya Life Insurance Company, so also, Mohan Jadekar was working in their office.
Within 10-15 minutes from the time of occurrence of the accident, he rushed to the spot, he did not witness as to who was riding the motorcycle and who was the pillion rider.
He called for ambulance from his mobile number and thereafter, injured were shifted to Lifeline Hospital at  16 Hubballi.
Karibasaveshwar Jadekar has also admitted that he has taken treatment in the hospital.
Since this witness has not supported the case of the respondent, he was treated as hostile and with the permission of the Court, he was cross
-examined.
Even during the cross-examination also the respondent has not elucidated any evidence from him to substantiate the defence set up by the Insurance Company.
21. RW2, Allamaprabhu Kubasad, Assistant Administrative Officer at National Insurance Company Limited, testified that there was a delay of one day in filing the complaint.
He disputed the manner of the accident as described in the police documents and contended that it resulted from the deceased's own rash and negligent driving of the motorcycle.

According to him, a delayed complaint was lodged in collusion between the alleged The Divisional Manager vs Sri. Aravind Gajanan Apte on 15 September, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/29919585/
13 motorcycle rider and its owner, with the claimants putting forth a false claim.

sentences.text: He argued that Karibasaveshwar Jadekar was not the motorcycle rider in question; rather, the accident occurred due to the deceased's negligent riding.

Furthermore, RW2 highlighted that despite the appellant summoning both the inpatient and out-patient case- sheets of Karibasaveshwar Jadekar, the hospital authorities only provided the OPD case sheet.
The MLC (Medico-Legal Case) and death notifications from Lifeline Hospital to Gokul Road Police Station indicated that the deceased was brought to the hospital by Anand Sajjan.
However, during cross-examination, RW1 (Anand Sajjan) stated that he did not transport Jadekar to the hospital, and only the deceased was taken to the hospital in his car.
This contrasted with the complaint's content, which asserted that both the deceased and Karibasaveshwar Jadekar were transported to the hospital together.
23. RW2 continued by pointing out inconsistencies between the injuries described in the complaint and those noted in the injury certificate.

He also highlighted that the Investigation Officer had submitted a final report to the Court,
naming Anand Sajjan as CW7.
However, RW1, who was examined as a witness before the Tribunal, explicitly stated that he had refused to provide a statement to the police in the police  18

14 station and had not given any statement to them.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Addressing Karibasaveshwar Jadekar's hospital admission, RW2 noted that he had been admitted to the hospital on 09th April, 2023, and remained there on 10th April, 2013, in an unconscious state.
However, medical records indicated that he was treated as an outpatient and was not admitted to the hospital.
This inconsistency was emphasized to cast doubt on the accuracy of the belated complaint.

24. RW2 proceeded to present the complete inpatient case sheet of Sunil Aravind Apte obtained from Lifeline Hospital (marked as Exhibit R4), along with the MLC extract (Exhibit R4(a)) dated 09th April, 2013, and the case sheet of Sunil Apte (Exhibit R4).
The intimation regarding Sunil Apte's death was marked as Exhibit R4(c).
During cross-examination, RW2 acknowledged that Exhibit P1 complaint indicated that Jadekar was the motorcycle rider responsible for the accident due to his negligence.
RW2 further confirmed that the Investigation Officer had filed a charge sheet against Karibasaveshwar Jadekar.

In the course of proceedings, RW3, Ramanagouda A.
Hatti, the Deputy Superintendent of Police, Dharwad, testified about the formal filing of a charge sheet against the motorcyclist-RW4, Dr. Yallappa B. Dambal, a Medical Practitioner, asserted that Karibasaveshwar Jadekar was not The Divisional Manager vs Sri. Aravind Gajanan Apte

on 15 September, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/29919585/
15 registered as an inpatient at Lifeline Hospital on 09th April, 2013,
supporting this claim with an exhibit that detailed in-patient records from 3rd to 15th April, 2013 and RW5, Mahammad Basha, an Engineer at the Bankapur Toll Plaza, confirmed that he was called upon to provide data and video specifics pertaining to vehicle KA-22/N-7112; however, he clarified that he possessed no information related to the said vehicle.

26. On perusal of the entire evidence placed on record by the appellant-Insurance Company, the same will only substantiate the case of the respondent-claimants for the reason that soon after the accident, Sunil Apte, was admitted to Lifeline 24/7 Hospital, Hubballi with the history of Road Traffic Accident.

The entire case sheet produced by the respondent-claimants reveal that the deceased was admitted to hospital on 09th April,
 20 2013 with the history of Road Traffic Accident and cause of death is shown as Head Injury  brainstem dysfunction and died at 12.25 am on 14th April, 2013.

27. The collective evidence of RWs.1 to 5 and the documents submitted by the appellant-Insurance Company,
marked as Exhibits R1 to R10, substantially corroborate the claimant-respondents' case.
These materials reflect that the deceased was admitted to the hospital immediately after the accident with a recorded history of a road traffic accident.
This evidence underscores his injuries resulting from the incident.

The Divisional Manager vs Sri. Aravind Gajanan Apte on 15 September, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/29919585/
16

entities.text: Divisional Manager vs Sri. Aravind Gajanan Apte
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The very evidence presented by RW1 itself confirms the injuries sustained in the road traffic accident.

The Investigating Officer,
responsible for the case investigation, has provided clear evidence regarding his inquiry and the subsequent submission of a charge sheet against the motorcycle's rider.

Had the deceased been riding the motorcycle during the accident, RW1-Anand Sajjan, the Senior Manager of Kotak Mahindra Insurance Company, who arrived at the scene within a short span of 10-15 minutes, would have filed a complaint with the relevant police  21 station due to the cognizable nature of the offence.

However,
RW1 did not initiate any such complaint.
The appellant- Insurance Company has failed to present credible legal evidence to support their defence.
Conversely, the claimant/respondents have effectively substantiated their argument through both oral and documentary evidence before the Tribunal.
28. With careful consideration of the evidence presented by both parties, the Tribunal appropriately evaluated the available evidence in accordance with legal principles.
This evaluation led to the determination that the accident resulted from the motorcycle rider's reckless and negligent conduct.
Even upon re-evaluation of the records, no legal flaws or irregularities in the Tribunal's findings regarding this matter are apparent.

In this case, no evidence of fraud as alleged by the appellant- Insurance Company has been identified, render the relied-upon The Divisional Manager vs Sri. Aravind Gajanan Apte on 15 September, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/29919585/
17 decision cited by the appellant's counsel inapplicable.

entities.text: Divisional Manager vs Sri. Aravind Gajanan Apte

sentences.text: As a result, we respond to point No.1 in the negative.

29 . As regards compensation is concerned, the Tribunal,
after appreciating the material on record considering the  22 documents produced by the respondent-claimants, has awarded the compensation of Rs.20,16,705/- with interest at 6% per annum from the date of petition till the date of payment.
We consider, the same is just and proper and does not call for any interference in this appeal.

In the result, we pass the following:
 ORDER 1. Appeal is dismissed;
2. The Judgment and award dated 25th July, 2019 passed in MVC No.349 of 2013 by the Principal Senior Civil Judge and Additional Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Hubballi is confirmed;
3. Amount in deposit if any, be transmitted to the Tribunal forthwith for onward disbursal of the same to the claimants.

Tragically, due to a severe head injury accompanied by brainstem dysfunction, he  4 succumbed to injuries on 14th April, 2013, while still under hospital care.
Prior to this devastating accident, the deceased enjoyed robust health.
The petitioner's elder brother, residing separately with his own family and children, did not share this burden.
4.2 The sudden loss of the family's primary source of income has subjected the petitioners to considerable mental anguish and distress.
Importantly, at the time of the accident, the deceased was 27 years old, known  5 for his brilliance, diligence, and exemplary qualities.
Additionally, he was on the cusp of marriage, which adds to the tragedy of his untimely passing.
Their claim rests on the premise that the negligent and reckless conduct of the rider of motorcycle-Karibasaveshwar Jadekar, directly contributed to the demise of Sunil.
The compensation sought encompasses medical expenses, loss of Sunil's income, and the profound emotional distress endured by the petitioners due to the sudden loss of their son.
The vehicle in question involved in the accident was examined by the Motor Vehicle Inspector; Investigation Officer has recorded the statement of witnesses; obtained post-mortem report and on thorough investigation, Investigating Officer has submitted the charge- sheet against the rider of the motorcycle bearing registration No.KA-25/Y-0784 for commission of offence punishable under Sections 279, 337, 304A of Indian Penal Code read with Section  14 134 and 187 of the Motor Vehicles Act.
